content: Nagios/Icinga soft vs hard state: a non-OK result enters SOFT state and is re-checked up to max_check_attempts; only after the retries confirm does it become HARD and notify. Explicit purpose per Nagios docs is 'to prevent false alarms from transient problems.' Event handlers may run during SOFT state to proactively fix before it becomes HARD. Operational advice when false alarms occur: raise max_check_attempts. This is the canonical N-consecutive-confirmations debounce and maps directly to 'confirm death after N consecutive frames'.
